senses.gloss: (cmp. קום, Gen. XXIII, 17) to create; to acquire, own; to take possession.
units: <cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 31a:2">R. Hash. 31ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Psalms 24">Ps. XXIV</cite> recited in the Temple on the first day of the week) <he>על שם שק׳ והקנה וכ׳</he> because he (the Lord in establishing the world) took possession and gave (his creatures) possession (invested them with a fief), and became the sovereign of the world.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kiddushin 1:1">Kidd. I, 1</cite> <he>האשה קוֹנָה את עצמה וכ׳</he> a wife acquires herself (becomes independent) when she receives her divorce &c.
<cite ref="Kiddushin 20a:15">Ib. 20ᵃ</cite> <he>כל הקוֹנֶה … כקונה וכ׳</he> whoever buys a Hebrew bondman creates, as it were, a master over himself.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 75b:12">B. Mets. 75ᵇ</cite> <he>הקונה אדון לעצמו</he> he who creates a master over himself, expl. <he>תולה נכסיו בנכרי</he> who (in order to evade obligations) hangs his property on a gentile (pretends to be merely the agent of a gentile); (another explan.) <he>הכותב נכסיו וכ׳</he> who transfers his property to his children during his lifetime.

<cite ref="Gittin 37b:19">Gitt. 37ᵇ</cite> sq. (ref. to <cite ref="Leviticus 25:45">Lev. XXV, 45</cite>) <he>אתם קוֹנִים וכ׳</he> you may buy (as a slave) one of them, but they cannot buy one of you, nor can they buy of one another.

<cite ref="Leviticus 25:45">Ib.</cite> <he>יכול לא יִקְנוּ זה את זה למעשה ידיו</he> you may think, they cannot buy one another for the work (as long as the serf choses to be in the master’s power); <he>ולא הם קוֹנִים … לגופו</he> they cannot buy of one another a bodily slave (who requires formal manumission to be a freeman).
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 46b:9">B. Mets. 46ᵇ</cite> bot. <he>מכור לי באלו ק׳</he> if one says, sell me (a certain object) for these (coins which I hold in my hand), he has bought (the sale is valid).
<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Metzia 4:1">Ib. IV, 1</cite> <he>הזהב קונה וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="G00080"><he>זָהָב</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Metzia 4:1">Ib.</cite> <he>מעות הרעות קוֹנוֹת וכ׳</he> the delivery of cancelled coins effects the purchase of the valid coins. Ib. 47ᵇ <he>מעות קונות</he> the delivery of the purchasing money gives possession (no formal possession of the purchased object (<cite ref="M02879"><he>מְשִׁיכָה</he></cite>) being required).
<cite ref="Kiddushin 22b">Kidd. 22ᵇ</cite> <he>הגבהה קונה</he> lifting up the purchased object makes the sale binding; a. v. fr.

senses.gloss: to make sure; to obligate a person by a special symbolical act (קִנְיָן); to enter into an obligation by a special symbolical form.
units: <cite ref="Gittin 51a:8">Gitt. 51ᵃ</cite> <he>בשקָנוּ מידו</he> when they (the court, witnesses &c.) made him obligate himself (that his widow should receive support from his estate); <he>בשקנו לזו ולא קנו לזו</he> when such an obligation was entered with reference to this (his wife’s case), but not with reference to that (his daughter’s case).

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 47a:10-11">B. Mets. 47ᵃ</cite> <he>במה קונין … בכליו של קונה</he> wherewith is the bargain made sure?… By handing over one of the garments (or any object) belonging to the purchaser; <he>דניחא ליה לקונה דליהוי מקנה קונה וכ׳</he> for the purchaser likes the seller to obligate himself, in order that he may be sure to give him possession; a. fr.—Ib. 48ᵇ when he said to him, <he>ערבוני יָקוּן</he> (fr. <cite ref="S00412"><he>קון</he></cite> = <he>קנה</he>) my earnest money shall serve to make the purchase sure.—Part. pass. <cite ref="S01543"><he>קָנוּי</he></cite>; f. <he>קְנוּיָה</he>; pl. <he>קְנוּיִים</he>, <he>קְנוּיִין</he>; <cite ref="S01941"><he>קְנוּיוֹת</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Kiddushin 16a:13">Kidd. 16ᵃ</cite> <he>עבד עברי גופו ק׳ והרב וכ׳</he> a Hebrew bondman is owned bodily (to the end of his term), and if the master allowed him a reduction of his time, his allowance is not legally binding (the slave not being able to acquire himself); <cite ref="Kiddushin 28a:6">ib. 28ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Bava Kamma 113b:1">B. Kam. 113ᵇ</cite>.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 86:3">Gen. R. s. 86</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Genesis 39:1">Gen. XXXIX, 1</cite>) <he>הקנויין קונין וכל וכ׳</he> as a rule those who are owned make themselves owners (slaves enrich themselves by robbing their master), and all slaves cause decrease to their master’s house, but in this case ‘the Lord blessed &c.’ (ib. 5); Yalk. ib. 145 <he>הקונין קונין</he> (corr. acc.); a. fr.—

<cite ref="Tosefta Nedarim 4:6">Tosef. Ned. IV, 6</cite> <he>קונם … שאני קנוי</he> the axe of which I am possessed be forbidden (v. <cite ref="S00446"><he>קוֹנָם</he></cite>), i.e. I swear that I have no axe; <cite ref="Nedarim 35a:1">Ned. 35ᵃ</cite> (Rashi <he>שאינו ק׳</he> I swear that another axe is not owned by me).—[<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Peah 4:3:6">Y. Peah IV, 18ᵇ</cite> <he>השעה קנויה</he>, read: <cite ref="Q01167"><he>פְּנוּיָה</he></cite>, v. <cite ref="Q01167"><he>פָּנוּי</he></cite>.]

<cite ref="Kiddushin 20a:17">Kidd. 20ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Leviticus 25:14">Lev. XXV, 14</cite>) <he>דבר הנ׳ מיד ליד</he> this refers to what is bought from hand to hand (movable goods). Ib. I, 1 <he>האשה נִקְנֵית וכ׳</he> a wife can be acquired in three ways. Ib. 6ᵇ <he>אין אשה נ׳ בחליפין</he> a wife cannot be taken possession of by symbolical delivery (<cite ref="H01058"><he>חֲלִיפִין</he></cite>). Ib. I, 3 <he>עבד כנעני נ׳ בכסף וכ׳</he> a Canaanite slave is taken possession of (is considered owned) either by delivery of the purchasing money, or by a deed, or by undisturbed possession (<cite ref="H00556"><he>חֲזָקָה</he></cite>). Ib. 5 <he>נכסים שיש … נִקְנִין וכ׳</he> landed property is acquired by means of handing over the money &c., but movables cannot be acquired otherwise than by taking hold (<cite ref="M02879"><he>מְשִׁיכָה</he></cite>). Ib. 22ᵇ <he>תִּקָּנֶה בביאה</he> let her be acquired (become his slave) by coition; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to give possession, sell, transfer. R. Hash. l. c., v. supra.
units: <cite ref="Sanhedrin 81b:19">Snh. 81ᵇ</cite> <he>ולמַקְנוֹ</he>, v. <cite ref="S00424"><he>קוֹנֶה</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Ketubot 82b:3">Keth. 82ᵇ</cite> <he>אשה הִקְנוּ לו וכ׳</he> it is heaven that gave him a wife (through his brother’s death without issue); <cite ref="Yevamot 39a:7">Yeb. 39ᵃ</cite>.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 47a:11">B. Mets. 47ᵃ</cite> <he>בכליו של מַקְנֶה</he>, v. supra.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 33b">Ib. 33ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>אין אדם מקנה דבר וכ׳</he> none can give possession of (sell) what does not yet exist (future crops &c.); a. fr.—Esth. R. introd. (ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 28:68">Deut. XXVIII, 68</cite> sq.) <he>למה ואין קונה … ע״י שלא הִקְנִיתֶם אלה וכ׳</he> why ‘no purchaser’?… Because you have not transmitted ‘these words of the covenant’, for there is none among you making the five books of the Law his own (v. <cite ref="S00424"><he>קוֹנֶה</he></cite>).
